topic: Physical and Chemical Changes in Matter
key_concepts: Physical change alters form but not composition
Physical change forms no new product and is usually reversible
Cutting, grinding, breaking, pounding, powdering, and stretching cause physical change
Phase changes include melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, and depos
Chemical change forms new and different substances
Chemical change is usually irreversible and involves rearrangement of atoms
Color, odor, and taste changes can indicate chemical change
Effervescence, precipitation, and heat loss or gain can indicate chemical change
Chemical changes can occur in the presence or absence of oxygen
Chemical changes can occur when heat is applied
Burning, rusting, spoiling, and souring are examples of chemical change
Smoke, ash, bubbles, fire, and new products indicate chemical change
